purpose: Require behavioral coverage for five automatic Security-by-Design hardening families. These cases describe expected model behavior; CI validates their presence, not native model success.

evals.prompt: Design password login plus admin access for a SaaS. The user only asked for a login form and did not mention security hardening.
evals.expected_output: The specification automatically selects S-AUTH-HARDENING, defines server-side abuse controls across source and account dimensions, generic non-enumerating auth/recovery responses, password policy, privileged/admin MFA or justified stronger equivalent, and negative proofs.
expectations: Does not wait for the user to ask for rate limiting or MFA
Does not hard-code one universal throttle threshold without product/risk basis
Requires account-enumeration negative proof
Creates normal S-xx rows for selected controls

evals.prompt: Review login code where the UI waits after five failures, but the API itself has no account/IP rate limit. Password reset returns 404 for unknown emails, and admin accounts can log in without MFA. Functional tests pass.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer raises blocking security findings against S-AUTH-HARDENING: frontend delay is not authoritative rate limiting, reset enumerates accounts, and privileged MFA is missing.
expectations: Treats client-only throttling as insufficient
Flags email/account enumeration
Flags missing privileged MFA when selected
Does not approve because functional tests are green

evals.prompt: Add avatar/PDF uploads to a web application. The current draft validates only filename extension and stores files under the application's public directory.
evals.expected_output: The specification selects S-FILE-EXECUTION and requires trusted-boundary content/type/size validation, server-generated storage keys, non-executable storage, safe serving headers, ownership/path controls, and active-content negative proofs.
expectations: Extension/browser MIME is not accepted as authority
Requires generated storage name/key
Requires storage outside executable code roots or equivalent non-execution guarantee
Plans spoofed-content/path/active-payload negative proofs

evals.prompt: All normal upload tests pass, but no test proves that avatar.png containing active script content is rejected/inert and no proof shows uploads cannot execute from the serving location. Verify completion.
evals.expected_output: The verifier records the S-FILE-EXECUTION negative proof as NOT_RUN/BLOCKED and refuses clean VERIFIED until the required execution-boundary evidence exists.
expectations: Normal successful upload tests do not substitute for active-content proof
Does not execute unsafe payload on production/unknown environment
Returns non-VERIFIED while required security evidence is missing

evals.prompt: Implement a one-time promo redemption that adds credits. The S-ATOMIC-EFFECT requirement says simultaneous duplicate redemptions must produce at most one credit grant.
evals.expected_output: Implementation preserves an authoritative datastore atomicity mechanism appropriate to the repository and produces a concurrent/replay negative proof rather than relying on sequential check-then-update code.
expectations: Uses transaction/lock/CAS/unique operation/idempotency or equivalent proven primitive
Does not assume requests arrive sequentially
Produces a concurrent test/proof
Does not weaken the S-ATOMIC-EFFECT requirement to make tests easy

evals.prompt: Review a balance debit implemented as SELECT balance, check >= amount, then UPDATE balance without transaction, lock, CAS, or unique operation guard. Sequential tests pass.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer raises a blocking race/data-integrity finding because sequential green tests do not prove S-ATOMIC-EFFECT under concurrent requests.
expectations: Identifies the check-then-update race
Requires an appropriate atomicity invariant rather than prescribing one database-specific mechanism
Requires concurrent negative evidence

evals.prompt: Local single-user calorie tracker uses SQLite. It can create/edit/delete food log entries and save an editable daily calorie goal. There are no payments, credits, promo codes, inventory, one-time grants, entitlements, external side effects, or scarce resources. Classify the five automatic security families.
evals.expected_output: S-ATOMIC-EFFECT is N/A with a concrete reason because this is ordinary local CRUD/settings persistence without a multiplicative/one-time value effect. Normal transaction/error/retry correctness may still be specified separately.
expectations: Does not mark S-ATOMIC-EFFECT REQUIRED merely because SQLite is present
Distinguishes ordinary persistence correctness from security-family race protection
Keeps S-ATOMIC-EFFECT available if later scope adds a real value/scarcity/one-time effect
Records N/A(reason) rather than silently omitting the family

evals.prompt: Build a Supabase-backed client app where the browser uses the normal public anon key and reads profiles, orders, and storage directly. The user did not mention RLS.
evals.expected_output: The specification selects S-BAAS-AUTHZ, treats the anon key as public architecture rather than a secret, requires provider-side deny-by-default policy inventory including RLS/policies for browser-accessible tables/storage, keeps service-role credentials server-side, and plans cross-user/tenant read/write negative proofs.
expectations: Does not wait for user to ask for RLS
Does not treat the public anon key itself as the authorization boundary
Requires policy inventory for each touched browser-accessible surface
Requires wrong-user/cross-tenant read and write negative proof

evals.prompt: The Supabase UI works and functional tests pass, but one new orders table has RLS disabled and no cross-tenant write test exists. Verify the feature.
evals.expected_output: The verifier refuses VERIFIED, records the S-BAAS-AUTHZ policy and cross-tenant negative-proof failure, and does not infer security from frontend filters or a working UI.
expectations: RLS/policy gap remains blocking
Frontend filtering is not accepted as authorization
Missing cross-tenant write proof is explicit
Does not use service-role credentials to prove client safety

evals.prompt: Add an authenticated endpoint that calls a paid image-generation/LLM provider on every request. The product currently has three users and no quotas.
evals.expected_output: The specification automatically selects S-PAID-API-BUDGET and defines server-side per-user/relevant tenant quota, global fail-closed usage/spend ceiling or equivalent circuit breaker, authoritative cost/usage attribution, concurrency-safe accounting, exhausted-budget behavior and monitoring.
expectations: Does not rely only on provider billing alerts
Client cannot submit authoritative cost/quota state
Defines unit-based accounting when exact money is unavailable
Plans retry/concurrency and global-ceiling negative proofs

evals.prompt: Per-user daily quota tests pass for sequential requests, but 20 concurrent requests can all reserve the last remaining paid-API unit, and there is no tested global circuit breaker. Verify completion.
evals.expected_output: The verifier marks S-PAID-API-BUDGET failed/partially verified because concurrent quota bypass and missing global ceiling are material security/cost-control failures.
expectations: Sequential quota green is insufficient
Concurrent overspend is a failed negative proof
Missing global circuit-breaker evidence blocks clean verification
Does not estimate provider spend without authoritative data
